claim.supported_scope: Deterministic indexed case resampling for supported OLS and binary logistic coefficients with fixed two-sided 95 percent standard-normal bootstrap-ratio tests, percentile-primary intervals, conditional BCa intervals, failure accounting, progress, cancellation, persistence, and native export.
claim.estimand: Sampling uncertainty for supported OLS and binary-logistic coefficient and odds-ratio point estimates under case resampling.
assumptions: Complete cases are exchangeable sampling units for the requested regression model.
At least 90 percent of requested resamples produce usable fits under the documented failure policy.
BCa inference is available only when every required delete-one fit is usable and its acceleration is estimable.
exclusions: Generic PLS-PM bootstrapping, PROCESS bootstrapping, studentized intervals, custom alpha or tails, and permutation inference are excluded.
Case weights, clustered sampling, categorical auto-encoding, and multinomial or ordinal logistic regression are excluded.
QuickPLS does not claim numerical identity with SmartPLS random-number streams.
warnings: Failed bootstrap and jackknife fits remain visible and are never silently discarded from qualification accounting.
A BCa interval may be unavailable even when the primary percentile interval is available.

references.citation: Efron (1979), Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
Hyndman and Fan (1996), Sample Quantiles in Statistical Packages
Independent Python and R reconstruction of the frozen indexed regression-bootstrap summaries

simulations.design: Frozen 140-row listwise OLS and binary-logistic fixture with exact QuickPLS witness reconstruction plus independently seeded Python and R case-resampling reconstructions.
simulations.seed_policy: Fixed QuickPLS witness seed and separately fixed independent Python and R seeds; indexed QuickPLS replicates are reduced in replicate order.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Exact witness arithmetic differs by at most 5e-11, every frozen Python/R distribution-parity threshold passes, and worker-count scientific payloads are exactly equal.

simulations.design: Single-class resamples, rank-deficient resamples, OLS residual-degree-of-freedom and HC3 failures, incomplete jackknife sets, degenerate standard errors, and below-90-percent usable cases.
simulations.seed_policy: Deterministic named fixtures plus frozen indexed resampling streams.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Every failed fit is accounted for, BCa unavailability is tagged exactly, and a below-threshold or cancelled run commits no partial result.

boundaries.case: Fewer than 90 percent of requested bootstrap fits are usable, an OLS resample has nonpositive residual degrees of freedom or undefined HC3 covariance, or the bootstrap standard error is degenerate.
boundaries.expected_behavior: OLS fit failures retain a typed reason and count against the usable-fit threshold; the run fails or the affected inference row is tagged unavailable according to the frozen policy, with no NaN or fabricated statistic emitted.

boundaries.case: The recipe requests a regression family or inference option outside supported OLS and binary logistic v1 scope.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Setup is blocked before resampling with the unsupported option identified.

boundaries.case: Dataset rows are consistently reordered while semantic observations remain the same.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Point estimates remain mapped correctly and distributional checks remain within the frozen tolerance; deterministic equality is required only for the same row order and seed.

boundaries.case: The same data, recipe, and seed are executed with different supported worker counts.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Replicate identities, failures, summaries, intervals, and analytical payloads are exactly equal.

boundaries.case: A replicate index, coefficient, failure, interval, witness, seed, method identity, or dataset fingerprint is altered after execution.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict archive validation rejects the complete changed result.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject a result whose capability identity differs from its recipe.
Reject a result relabeled as another regression-bootstrap method version.
Reject a result whose saved dataset fingerprint no longer matches.
Reject any modified archive entry whose checksum no longer matches.
Reject duplicated keys, unknown fields, non-finite values, invalid indices, incomplete partitions, or inconsistent summaries.
Never reinterpret point-only, PLS-bootstrap, PROCESS-bootstrap, or legacy regression output as regression_bootstrap_v1.

persistence.legacy_policy: Point-only and unrelated resampling payloads remain readable under their original identities and cannot be promoted as regression-bootstrap evidence.

native.gui_cli_parity_rule: For the same dataset, recipe, seed, and worker count, GUI and CLI analytical payloads must be exactly equal apart from operational timestamps; scientific output must also be worker-invariant.
accessibility_rules: Bootstrap distributions have equivalent accessible summary tables.
Failure counts, unavailable intervals, warnings, and provenance are available without color or pointer interaction.
